prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1239; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A dated repair quote from before the policy start shows this same damage already existed.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported rear-end collision received and assigned for review. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.
Entry 2: Vehicle inspection scheduled. The damage to the rear of the claimant's vehicle appears consistent with the impact described in the first report.
Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision and lists the other driver's account.
Entry 4: Photographs taken at the scene were reviewed. They confirm some details of the damage and positioning, but no independent witnesses have come forward.
Entry 5: Claimant's counsel submitted a medical summary describing neck and back strain. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type and speed.
Entry 6: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. The account matches the one given at first notice and in the follow-up call with the adjuster.
Entry 7: Records check completed. No prior injury to the same body area is known, and no earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our file.
Entry 8: Repair estimate from before the policy start was located in the file. It lists damage to the same rear panels, which conflicts with the claimant's account that the vehicle was undamaged beforehand.
Entry 9: Referred the repair estimate discrepancy to the supervisor for review. Requested an explanation from counsel and the original repair facility.
Entry 10: Treatment records received. Care followed a typical course, with physical therapy and medication, and symptoms eased steadily as the claimant improved.
Entry 11: Verified the insured driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force at the time of loss. Coverage confirmed for the reported incident.
Entry 12: File reviewed with the supervisor. The injury claim remains open pending counsel's response on the prior repair estimate and a final review of the treatment billing.
